title: The Choir of the Glass Steppe Revisited
premise: Petra Villalobos, a royal food-taster whose body has been slowly immunized against poison for five years, hides a second secret: they are a hedge-witch selling forbidden charms in a city where magic is punishable by drowning. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, Petra learns the wards were powered by a covenant between the human realm and the star-spirits—a covenant broken by the crown itself to hoard magic for the throne. Hunted by the Inquisitor who once spared them, Petra must gather the scattered remnants of the old choir of mages and journey across the Glass Steppe to the starless shrine where the covenant was first sung. The story ends with Petra choosing justice over restoration: rather than reforge the covenant as it was, they sing a new one that dissolves the monarchy's monopoly on magic, at the cost of their own immunity—and nearly their life—leaving the stars dim but returning, and the city forever changed.
about_author: Lior Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing outlawed folk-magic traditions before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town, accompanied by an opinionated cat and an ever-growing collection of half-remembered lullabies.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet them mid-service in the royal kitchens, detecting nightshade in the queen's stew while concealing the charm-stitch in their sleeve. A flashback establishes the drowning of their mentor five years ago. Emotional beat: the exhausting discipline of being invisible, and the quiet grief beneath competence.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At midnight the border wards shatter like struck glass and every star above the city goes dark; panic spreads through the markets where Petra's charms suddenly glow uncontrollably, marking their customers. The Inquisitor Casimir Vane appears at their door—not arresting, but asking questions. Emotional beat: terror of exposure tangled with a strange relief that hiding is finally over.

chapters.title: What the Crown Buried
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Through his interrogation-adjacent conversations with Petra, we learn the wards were fed by the covenant, and that the king's grandfather broke it deliberately, caging star-fire beneath the palace. Casimir is torn between duty and the evidence he can no longer unsee. Emotional beat: a man of law discovering the law itself is the crime.

chapters.title: Charmsellers and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Fleeing arrest after a customer betrays them, Petra seeks out the last members of the old choir: a disgraced court musician, a deaf bone-carver, and a child who remembers songs she was never taught. Each carries a fragment of the covenant's melody. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership—Petra never wanted followers.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The group retrieves the covenant's first verse from the riverbed where executed mages were drowned; the dead do not rest quietly, and the bone-carver pays a price to bargain with them. Casimir, following, witnesses the rite and chooses not to report it. Emotional beat: communion with the dead, and the cost of asking ghosts for help.

chapters.title: Crossing the Steppe
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The company crosses the Glass Steppe under a starless sky, pursued by ward-hounds bred from the stolen star-fire. Supplies fail; the child's song grows stronger as they near the shrine, and Petra's charms begin answering her instead of them. Emotional beat: endurance fraying into doubt—is the covenant worth what it's costing?

chapters.title: The Shrine Without Sky
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. At the ruined shrine, the group finds the king's own envoy already there, offering Petra pardon and title if they reforge the covenant under crown control. The musician accepts; the bone-carver refuses and is taken. Petra realizes restoration means replacing one cage with another. Emotional beat: temptation, betrayal, and the hard birth of conviction.

chapters.title: A Song With No Owner
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra proposes the unthinkable: not restoring the old covenant but singing a new one that belongs to no throne, dispersing magic to everyone or no one. The choir rehearses in secret while Casimir, now openly traitor, buys them one night by burning the envoy's dispatches. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At dawn the crown's forces descend as the choir begins the new song; the ward-hounds turn on their masters; the envoy kills the musician; Petra pours their hard-won poison-immunity into the covenant as its price, collapsing as the first stars flicker back. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, chaos, and the terrifying moment before the sky answers.

chapters.title: Dim Stars, Returning
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, weeks later. Petra survives, weakened, their immunity gone—now an ordinary taster in a city where magic is ordinary too. The monarchy limps on, diminished; Casimir resigns his office to teach the new songs. On the steppe, the stars burn low but steady. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—justice achieved not as triumph, but as a shared, fragile inheritance.
